question: A 33-year-old pregnant woman in the 28th week of gestation presents to the emergency department for evaluation of bilateral edema of her legs. It seems to worsen at the end of the day and has lasted for the past 3 weeks. History reveals that this is her 3rd pregnancy. Vital signs include: blood pressure 120/80 mm Hg, heart rate 74/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and temperature 36.6°C (98.0°F). Body mass index is 36 kg/m2. Physical examination reveals bilateral leg edema with engorged surface veins. A photograph of the patient’s legs is shown. Which of the following is the best initial management of the patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pregnancy" -> "Increased risk of venous insufficiency" -> "Bilateral leg edema" -> "Compression stockings recommended as initial management" -> 95% CHAIN: "Pregnancy" -> "Increased blood volume and pressure on lower extremities" -> "Bilateral leg edema" -> "Compression stockings recommended as initial management" -> 95%
analysis: The patient is a pregnant woman with bilateral leg edema, which is likely due to venous insufficiency exacerbated by pregnancy. The best initial management for her would be conservative measures to alleviate symptoms and improve venous return.
